title: 14,555 inmates escaped
statement: The commission report records the escape of 14,555 inmates from various prisons.
verification_note: Ratopati summary of the commission.

title: 19 killed in Kathmandu on 8 September
statement: At least 19 people were killed in Kathmandu on 8 September.
verification_note: Amnesty (Dec) and the BBC report (via Onlinekhabar) place 19 deaths in Kathmandu. HRW (Nov), CIVICUS, Kathmandu Post and others give 17 in Kathmandu plus 2 in Itahari, which makes 19 nationwide. HRW (9 Sept) and Al Jazeera give 19 without a geographic split.

title: 196 injured still under care at 32 hospitals
statement: On 19 September 2025, 196 people injured in the protests were receiving care at 32 hospitals, 28 at the National Trauma Centre, and the government would reimburse treatment fees.
verification_note: Based on Health Emergency Operation Centre data under the Ministry of Health and Population, as quoted by the Kathmandu Post.

title: 2024 floods: at least 219 dead
statement: The September 2024 floods and landslides killed at least 219 people and displaced over 12,000 families.
verification_note: See the 224 and 249 claims.

title: 2024 floods: at least 224 dead
statement: At the 1 Oct 2024 count the September 2024 floods and landslides had killed 224 people and injured 158, with 24 missing.
verification_note: Competing tolls for the same event: 217 (URL of the AP story), 219 (Global Voices), 224 (AP text), 249 (Nepal Economic Forum, 2025). Counting date and categories are not stated.

title: 2024 floods: 249 dead
statement: The flooding led to 249 deaths, 177 injuries and the displacement of more than 10,000 families.
verification_note: A later total than the AP and Global Voices figures; the source does not say what it counts.

title: 26 platforms were blocked
statement: Twenty-six platforms were blocked. Other counts reported are "about two dozen" (AP) and 27 (India Today). The Kathmandu Post names the seven exceptions but gives no total.
verification_note: 26 appears in Guardian, BBC, Al Jazeera, HRW, Global Voices and Onlinekhabar. India Today says 27 "unregistered" sites; AP says "about two dozen". No retrieved source lists all platforms; the full list was not published in the sources found.

title: Claim that 32 protesters or children were detained, disappeared or killed inside Parliament
statement: Claims circulated that 32 Gen Z protesters, described in one version as children, had been detained or had disappeared inside the Parliament building and that their bodies were later found.
verification_note: Assessment: false. The Diplomat Nepal calls the claim false; IPS describes a version in which police detained 32 children inside Parliament and the children were killed there, and calls it false. Neither source names a recovered body count matching the claim.

title: At least 33 killed by live bullets
statement: The Tribhuvan University Institute of Medicine's forensic department found at least 33 killed protesters were struck by live bullets from high-velocity firearms; of 34 bodies with bullet wounds, 10 were hit in the head, 18 in the chest, 4 in the stomach and 2 in the neck.
scope: bodies examined at the TU Institute of Medicine forensic department
figure_more: 34 bodies with bullet wounds: 10 head; 18 chest; 4 stomach; 2 neck
verification_note: Single report by Reuters; bullets were distorted so calibre could not be determined.

title: 74 deaths nationwide
statement: Reuters, on 26 September 2025, put the overall death toll at 74 with more than 2,000 injured.
verification_note: Earlier tally than the 76 and 77 figures; it may predate later deaths. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': An earlier tally (26 September), not a conflicting one.

title: 76 deaths nationwide
statement: At least 76 people were killed nationwide in the unrest of 8 and 9 September.
verification_note: HRW and Amnesty give 76 (Amnesty counts the two-day protests and six days of unrest); AFP gives 77 for 8 to 9 September; Reuters' forensic report gives 74 on 26 Sept.

title: 77 deaths nationwide
statement: At least 77 people were killed in the 8 and 9 September protests.
verification_note: AFP via News24, 27 Feb 2026.

title: AI-generated images and videos of Parliament and Singha Durbar burning circulated before the protests
statement: AI-generated photos and videos of Parliament and Singha Durbar being burned or destroyed circulated on social media before the 8 September 2025 protests.
verification_note: Kantipur, reporting the facts-and-analysis section of an official commission report (27 May 2026), and Onlinekhabar's one-year retrospective (8 September 2026) both state this. Onlinekhabar's October 2025 report on Cyabra says AI-generated images built momentum before the protest. Kantipur's retrievable text does not name the commission.

title: All Supreme Court records and evidence were destroyed (Sushila Karki)
statement: AFP quotes interim Prime Minister Sushila Karki saying 'All our records, evidence, files of the Supreme Court have been all destroyed.'
verification_note: Setopati and SCMP give file counts for the Supreme Court; engineers cited by Republica say hard drives were removed and sensitive-file rooms were targeted.

title: Ammunition 13182 rounds over two days
statement: 13,182 rounds were fired over 8 and 9 September: 2,642 live bullets, 1,884 rubber rounds and 6,279 tear-gas shells.
figure_more: 2,642 live bullets; 1,884 rubber rounds; 6,279 tear-gas shells
verification_note: Harvard's analysis; covers two days, so it cannot be assigned to 8 September alone.

title: Amnesty: 19 killed, 300+ injured at the 8 September assembly in Kathmandu
statement: Amnesty said at least 19 people were killed and more than 300 injured at the 8 September assembly in Kathmandu.
verification_note: HRW (19 November 2025) gives 17 killed in Kathmandu; HRW (9 September) gives 19 nationwide, which fits 17 in Kathmandu plus 2 in Itahari. Amnesty ties 19 to Kathmandu, so the scope may differ.

title: Nepal protest video shared as anti-Modi protests in India
statement: Videos of protests in Nepal were shared with captions saying that India was in turmoil and that Narendra Modi's government faced protests.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Rumor Scanner located one video in Nepalgunj (B.P. Chowk) during the 9 September 2025 protests and ran a second check on a similar caption. Both checks are by the same publisher.

title: Army chief allegedly asked President Paudel to step aside
statement: A senior journalist wrote on X that the army chief allegedly asked President Paudel to step aside so the military could negotiate, and that the President replied "I will not resign". Nepali Times adds that the army was criticised for detaining the President and not letting him take part in the talks.
verification_note: Relayed by Nepali Times as an allegation; no other outlet retrieved repeats it and the army did not comment in the retrieved sources.

title: Video said to show Army Chief Sigdel saying the king should be placed at the centre
statement: A video shared in 2026 carried the claim that Army Chief Ashok Raj Sigdel said the country was in a sensitive state and the king should be placed at the centre.
verification_note: Result given: misleading. Newschecker Nepal says the video was an older clip posted in January 2026 and there is no evidence that Sigdel made the statement.

title: Fabricated statement attributed to Army Chief Sigdel (March 2025)
statement: A statement attributed to Army Chief Ashok Raj Sigdel said: 'Nepal Army has finally made its position clear. We are the soldiers of the nation but not the government. We are ready to abide by the people's decision.'
verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal says the Army spokesperson confirmed the army did not issue it. A retired Indian Army major general shared a screenshot on X on 9 March 2025, the day thousands of pro-monarchy supporters welcomed former King Gyanendra Shah in Kathmandu. Build-up period.

title: Army delayed mobilisation on 9 September
statement: The commission recommended action against military commanders who delayed army mobilisation while important structures burned.
verification_note: Ratopati summary of the commission report. HRW places the army's deployment at around 10 p.m.; the army was already at New Baneshwar on 8 September.

title: Army plans to take over and restore the monarchy
statement: Media reports and social media rumours on 11-12 September said the army was likely to take over and reinstate the monarchy, and that former King Gyanendra was trying to stage a comeback. The army issued a notice denying it and its chief told embassy attaches it was not a coup.
verification_note: Rumour reported by ETV Bharat and Nepali Times; denied by the army's notice and by General Sigdel as quoted by The Kathmandu Post. Gyanendra rumours also debunked by Gen Z fact-checkers (see separate claim).

title: Army warned an emergency would be declared if no agreement
statement: The army chief reportedly warned on Friday 12 September that a state of emergency might have to be declared if no government was in place by evening, which helped to clinch the agreement on Karki.
verification_note: Border Lens attributes this to local media; Nepali Times and The Wire word it as "the military's warning" and "army officers apparently warned". No on-record army confirmation was retrieved.

title: Arrest warrants were issued by the court
statement: IANS and Tribune say the two were arrested after arrest warrants were issued by the court.
verification_note: Jurist says prosecutors had to ask a judge to validate urgent warrants on Sunday; OCCRP speaks of emergency warrants.

title: Arrest warrants were urgent and awaiting court validation
statement: Jurist says government prosecutors had to ask a judge on Sunday to validate the urgent arrest warrants.
verification_note: Conflicts with the report that the court had issued the warrants.

title: Arson at Singha Durbar, Kathmandu District Court and the Supreme Court was planned
statement: Engineers cited by Republica said the arsonists used petrol bottles and went straight to rooms with vital documents; at the Supreme Court hard drives were removed from intact computers.
verification_note: One source retrieved. The Karki commission recommends investigating those involved.

title: Balen Shah and Kulman Ghising declined the interim role
statement: Nepali Times says Shah and Ghising were considered but both declined, possibly because they want to contest the next elections. The Tribune (PTI) reported conflicting media reports that Ghising might be appointed prime minister, and Al Jazeera says moderators could not reach Shah.
verification_note: Reports conflict on whether Ghising was a live candidate; no direct statement from Shah or Ghising declining was retrieved. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'confirmed': The statement itself records the differing reports; no other claim or source disputes it.

title: Balen Shah endorsed Karki on Wednesday 10 September
statement: ANI reports that Kathmandu Mayor Balendra Shah posted on Facebook on Wednesday that he fully supported Karki leading the interim government. The Kathmandu Post (30 Sept) places Shah's support after Gen Z nominated Karki on 11 September at 7 pm.
verification_note: Timing differs by about a day between ANI/Onlinekhabar and the Post reconstruction; Al Jazeera (11 Sept) already reports Shah voicing support.

title: Claim that PM Balen Shah was set to reinstate the monarchy by removing the president (2026)
statement: A video claimed Prime Minister Balen Shah was all set to reinstate the monarchy by removing the president.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal, 31 March 2026, says the new government had made no such decision or preparation.

title: Claim that Balen Shah was appointed prime minister or head of state in September 2025
statement: In September 2025, TikTok and Facebook posts claimed Kathmandu mayor Balendra Shah had been appointed prime minister or head of state, one adding that activists had set fire to the prime minister's wife.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal found the video recycled from an earlier oath ceremony; Fact Crescendo found Shah held no national post and that Sushila Karki became interim prime minister.

title: Critics say the block was meant to stifle the anti-corruption campaign
statement: Critics say the block was an attempt to stifle the online anti-corruption and anti-nepotism campaign. The government denies this and describes it as regulation.
verification_note: BBC and Nepali Times report the critics’ view. Timing cuts against it: the Cabinet instruction (25 August) and the notice (28 August) predate the spread of nepo-kid content (first Nepal-focused TikTok video 2 September, Onlinekhabar). The government says it is enforcing a court directive and bringing platforms under Nepali law. No source shows the government’s intent either way.

title: Government: registration needed for tax and regulatory purposes
statement: The government said social media registration was necessary for tax and regulatory purposes; platforms had not registered by 3 September.
verification_note: Rights groups (CPJ, Amnesty, HRW) call the ban censorship or an unlawful restriction on expression.

title: Officials: ban needed to curb disinformation and criminal activity
statement: Officials said the ban on 26 platforms was necessary to curb disinformation and criminal activity (The Record).
verification_note: The Record reports unnamed officials; this stated reason differs from the tax and regulatory reason HRW reports. No verbatim anchor retrieved.

title: Ban lifted late monday night
statement: The government lifted the social media ban late on Monday night, 8 September.
verification_note: Al Jazeera says late Monday night. AFP datelines the announcement Tuesday, a day after the deaths. Possibly the same overnight decision reported on two dates.

title: Ban lifted on tuesday
statement: The government withdrew the social media ban on Tuesday, 9 September, after an emergency cabinet meeting.
verification_note: AFP (via Prothom Alo): the minister said the government withdrew the ban following an emergency cabinet meeting; blue News (Keystone-SDA) says late-night crisis meeting.

title: BBC documentary called one-sided
statement: Critics described the BBC documentary as one-sided and released a week before the election.
verification_note: Criticism as reported by Nepali Times, which also reports praise from supporters.

title: Bhat-Bhateni loss of NPR 10.85 billion (chairperson)
statement: Chairperson Min Bahadur Gurung reported losses of NPR 10.85 billion.
verification_note: The Kathmandu Post (September 2026) reports losses of more than Rs11 billion; insurance claims above Rs2.5 billion were reported on 14 September. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': Figures from September 2025 and September 2026; the later one is an update.

title: Bhat-Bhateni loss of more than NPR 11 billion
statement: The Kathmandu Post reports the company reported losses of more than Rs11 billion, with more than Rs500 million of goods looted.
figure_more: more than Rs500 million of goods looted
verification_note: Close to the NPR 10.85 billion figure given in September 2025. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': A later figure for the same loss; an update, not a conflict.

title: Bhatbhateni Chuchhepati: seven charred bodies (17 Sep)
statement: Seven charred bodies were recovered from the Chuchhepati Bhatbhateni outlet (Onlinekhabar and Republica, 17 Sep 2025), kept at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.
figure_more: kept at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital
verification_note: The Himalayan Times (14 Sep) and HRW say six. The 73rd death in the national count may be the seventh body.

title: Bhatbhateni Chuchhepati: six charred bodies (14 Sep)
statement: Police recovered six charred human remains from the burned Bhatbhateni Supermarket at Chuchhepati on 14 September 2025.
verification_note: Onlinekhabar and Republica (17 Sep) say seven were recovered at the same store.

title: Block took effect at midnight on Thursday 4 September
statement: The block took effect at midnight on Thursday 4 September 2025. Other accounts: from 4 September "today" (ministry), Friday evening (Swarajya), difficulty from Friday (BBC); AFP found platforms reachable on Thursday.
verification_note: Different reporters describe the order, the technical rollout and user experience, which may explain part of the gap. ISPs rolled out the block gradually (Onlinekhabar: "gradually blocked").

title: Critics say the block violates freedom of expression
statement: Rights groups, a Nepali Congress general secretary and commentators say the block breaches freedom of expression and the right to information. The government says it is not banning social media.
verification_note: Positions are attributed; no court has ruled on the block in the retrieved sources. Government position in BBC and AP.

title: Bluewin calls gurung home minister
statement: Prithvi Subba Gurung is the Home Minister.
verification_note: blue News (Keystone-SDA) calls Gurung 'Home Minister'. AFP via Prothom Alo calls him Minister for Communication, and Ramesh Lekhak was Home Minister until resigning on the evening of 8 September. Treat as a source error. No anchor for blue News because its text was paraphrased by the fetch tool.

title: Claim that businessman Durga Prasai played a central role in the protest
statement: Indian television channels suggested that the businessman Durga Parsai (as spelled by Decode) played a central role in the protest.
verification_note: Decode (BOOM) says the claim was publicly denied by the protesters. No independent check retrieved.

title: Cabinet decision on platform registration dated 25 August
statement: The Cabinet decision requiring platforms to register within one week was taken on 25 August 2025 (Onlinekhabar, Swarajya). Radio Nepal dates the Council of Ministers decision to 26 August.
verification_note: One-day difference between outlets; the decision text was not retrieved. Swarajya cites the Kathmandu Post and the minister, so it may share an origin with Onlinekhabar.

title: Cabinet expansion was done without consulting Gen Z
statement: Sudan Gurung's group said on 14 September that the cabinet expansion was done without consulting them and demanded Karki's resignation. The Kathmandu Post and Al Jazeera that day reported Karki consulting a core Gen Z group and Hami Nepal members meeting on posts.
verification_note: Gurung's group claims to speak for Gen Z; other Gen Z representatives were reported as consulted. Setopati notes the protesters "claim" to be leaders of the movement.

title: Cabinet, not the ministry, decided the 4 September block
statement: Onlinekhabar’s one-year piece says a Cabinet meeting on 4 September decided to shut the platforms. Kathmandu Post and Onlinekhabar on 4 September say a ministry meeting decided, after a 25 August Cabinet instruction to register.
verification_note: The two Onlinekhabar articles are a year apart. No Cabinet record for 4 September was found in the retrieved sources.

title: Cases against most protest accused cannot be withdrawn
statement: The Regmi committee found that charges can be withdrawn for about 300 of 1,778 people named in 445 cases; the rest face murder, arson or looting allegations that cannot be dropped under existing law, and property damage cases need complainant consent.
verification_note: One report as described by the Kathmandu Post.

title: CDO Rijal: he ordered rubber bullets below the knee, not final force
statement: Kathmandu Chief District Officer Chhabilal Rijal told the probe commission he gave a verbal order to fire rubber bullets targeted below the knee but did not give the order of final force.
verification_note: In the same statement Rijal said he heard on the police radio set that first the Inspector General of Police and then the acting chief of the Kathmandu Valley Police Office gave the order 'open fire as necessary to bring the situation under control'. BBC Eye Investigations (via Onlinekhabar) cites a police log with a 'use necessary force' order from 'Peter 1'. Both accounts name police commanders, not the CDO, as ordering lethal force; they are not independently confirmed.

title: 1,400 inmates escaped from the Central Prison, Sundhara (Republica)
statement: Republica reported 1,400 inmates escaped from the Central Prison in Sundhara.
verification_note: INSEC lists 3,003 for the Sundhara Central Jail.

title: 3,003 inmates escaped from the Central Jail, Sundhara (INSEC)
statement: INSEC reported 3,003 inmates escaped from the Central Jail in Sundhara, from a capacity of about 3,800.
verification_note: Republica lists 1,400 for the same prison.

title: Charge under Sections 181 and 182 of the Penal Code
statement: The commission recommended, and the arrests relate to, charges against Oli, Lekhak and Khapung under Sections 181 and 182 for criminal negligence, with up to 10 years' imprisonment (Jurist: three to ten years).
verification_note: Onlinekhabar instead reports sections 281, 282 and 283 of the Muluki Criminal Code with a maximum of three years and Rs 30,000.

title: Charge under Sections 281 to 283 of the Criminal Code
statement: Onlinekhabar reports Oli and Lekhak were arrested on charges of causing death through negligence under sections 281, 282 and 283, with a maximum of three years and a Rs 30,000 fine.
verification_note: Conflicts with the Sections 181-182 account used by the Kathmandu Post, Tribune and Jurist.

title: Child among the dead
statement: A 12-year-old child was among those killed by police fire.
verification_note: ANI via The Tribune only. No name is recorded in this dataset.

title: Indian TV claim that a China-US power struggle was behind the Nepal protests
statement: Times Now Navbharat said Nepal had been turned into an arena where the struggle for supremacy between China and America is taking place.
verification_note: Reported and criticised by Newslaundry (9 September 2025), which says the foreign-hand framing sidelined domestic causes. No evidence for the claim was retrieved.

title: Chinese social media users suspected a US and India role in the Nepal unrest
statement: Chinese social media users suspected that the United States, and India, were behind the unrest in Nepal, and one cited a US $500 million Millennium Challenge Corporation grant.
verification_note: StratNews Global (10 September 2025) records these as netizen opinions and adds no rebuttal or evidence.

title: Rajyalaxmi Chitrakar, wife of former prime minister Jhalanath Khanal, died on 9 September...
statement: Rajyalaxmi Chitrakar, wife of former prime minister Jhalanath Khanal, died on 9 September 2025 after protesters set fire to the family home in Dallu.
verification_note: Reported by TBS and other outlets citing family sources. BOOM, Alt News and Setopati reported she was alive and in critical or improving condition; Tribune India (23 September) and Kantipur (22 December) report later treatment in Delhi and her return home. The death report is contradicted.

title: Rajyalaxmi Chitrakar survived the fire with burn injuries, was treated in Kathmandu and th...
statement: Rajyalaxmi Chitrakar survived the fire with burn injuries, was treated in Kathmandu and then Delhi, and returned home.
verification_note: BOOM, Alt News, Setopati, Tribune India and Kantipur agree that she survived. Tribune reports 15 per cent burns and a damaged left hand.

title: Collateral damage of about NPR 3 trillion (economists)
statement: The Kathmandu Post quotes economists estimating the collateral damage at around Rs3 trillion, nearly equal to Nepal's budget for one and a half years.
verification_note: An economist's estimate that includes indirect effects; FNCCI and AFP give far lower totals for direct losses. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': Includes indirect effects; it measures something other than direct losses.

title: Commission recommends investigation of Oli, Lekhak, Khapung
statement: The commission recommended a criminal investigation of then PM KP Sharma Oli, then Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak and then IGP Chandra Kuber Khapung.
verification_note: Kantipur headline (retrieved page showed headline only). Ratopati's summary in a search result describes the grounds as criminal negligence; that wording was not retrieved as page text.

title: Commission report is about 1,000 pages
statement: The commission's report to Prime Minister Karki is 1,000 pages long.
verification_note: B360 Nepal and a search summary of newsonair say 1,000 pages; Setopati's summary says about 8,000-10,000 pages.

title: Commission report is 8,000-10,000 pages
statement: The report is about 8,000-10,000 pages long (Setopati's summary).
verification_note: Conflicts with the 1,000-page figure; Setopati may count annexes.

title: Commission: protests were incited through AI, fake police pages and hacking
statement: A commission report, as reported by Kantipur on 27 May 2026, says the protests were incited through AI-generated content, fake pages impersonating the police and hacking.
verification_note: Only the headline and first paragraph of the Kantipur article could be retrieved. Details of the fake police pages and hacking are not available in the retrieved text, and the commission is not named there. Not independently confirmed.

title: Parliamentary committee concluded Lamichhane was involved in cooperative fund misuse
statement: A parliamentary committee concluded that Rabi Lamichhane was involved in misusing cooperative funds funnelled into Gorkha Media Network, where he had been managing director.
verification_note: This records what the committee concluded, not a court finding; the Supreme Court on 23 May 2025 upheld his custody on the available evidence.

title: Crowdfunding for victims is slow to reach them
statement: Of 57 campaigns with a total target of Rs102.8 million, Rs25.87 million had been raised by 12 November 2025, and many victims and families had received no help.
figure_more: 57 campaigns with a target of Rs102.8 million
verification_note: Single Kathmandu Post analysis.

title: Viral video: crying man is Minister Gurung
statement: A viral video was shared as showing communication minister Prithvi Subba Gurung pleading with protesters.
verification_note: Newschecker says the man is not the minister; the uploader said he was a neighbour.

title: Curfew from 12 30 pm
statement: The Kathmandu district administration's curfew around New Baneshwar took effect at 12:30 pm and ran to 10 pm.
verification_note: Stated by Kathmandu Post, HRW, ANI/Tribune, Himalayan Times, Harvard and Onlinekhabar.

title: Curfew from 3 30 pm
statement: A curfew was in force from 3:30 pm.
verification_note: Kathmandu Post's 19-dead article gives 3:30 pm in a general sentence about authorities. Six outlets give 12:30 pm for Kathmandu. A later or wider curfew order may exist; none was found for Kathmandu.

title: Curfew imposed on Sunday afternoon
statement: Radio Nepal’s English report, dated 8 September, says a curfew was imposed in parts of Baneshwor on Sunday afternoon. Every other source dates the order to Monday 8 September.
verification_note: Almost certainly a wrong weekday in the Radio Nepal text, since its own dateline is 8 September (a Monday). Recorded as a source error.

title: Cyabra: about one third of online discourse on the protests came from fake accounts
statement: Cyabra, an Israel-based cyber intelligence firm, said in October 2025 that nearly 34 percent of online discourse during the 8 and 9 September protests was driven by fake accounts and AI-generated content.
verification_note: The two Nepali reports describe the same Cyabra analysis differently. Onlinekhabar says 34 percent of the online discourse was driven by fake accounts and AI content. Republica says fake accounts made up 34 percent of sampled profiles on X, that they generated 11.5 percent of engagements (over 164,000 interactions), and that genuine users drove the bulk of protest activity. The underlying Cyabra report was not retrieved, and the analysis is of a sample on X.

title: The residence of Pushpa Kamal Dahal was set on fire on 9 September 2025
statement: The residence of Pushpa Kamal Dahal was set on fire on 9 September 2025.
verification_note: Business Today says protesters set ablaze Dahal's residence without naming the place. Setopati says stones were thrown at the Khumaltar residence with some vandalism. Tribune says vandalised. Onlinekhabar reports arson at his Chitwan house, and Setopati reports a house of his daughter set on fire in Dholahiti. The reports may describe different houses.

title: Breakdown of 51 deaths: 30 gunshots, 21 burns and other injuries
statement: Of the 51 deaths reported by 13 September 2025, 30 were killed by gunshots and 21 died from burns, wounds and other injuries (Ministry of Health and Population, via ANI).
figure_more: 30 killed by gunshots; 21 died from burns, wounds and other injuries
verification_note: One ANI report.

title: Army breakdown of 76 deaths: 22 protesters, 3 police, 10 prisoners, 41 others
statement: At a press conference on 17 October 2025 the Nepali Army gave 22 protesters (shot by police), three police officers and 10 prisoners among the 76 dead, listing the remaining 41 as 'others' and suspecting looting, arson or self-started fires.
figure_more: 22 protesters shot by police; 3 police officers; 10 prisoners; 41 others
verification_note: Conflicts with the Chief Secretary's 59 protesters, 10 inmates and three security personnel (14 Sep). The Army's own category of 41 'others' is not defined in the sources, and 22 + 41 + 3 + 10 = 76.

title: Breakdown of 51 deaths by police: 21 protesters, 9 prisoners, 3 police, 18 others
statement: Police spokesperson Binod Ghimire said on 12 September 2025 that the dead included 21 protesters, nine prisoners, three police officers and 18 others.
verification_note: Al Jazeera and DW both relay the same police statement (DW credits AFP), so this is one origin.

title: Death toll: 14 killed by about 4 pm on 8 Sep
statement: As of about 4 pm on Monday 8 September 2025, at least 14 people had died after police opened fire at the Gen Z protest centred at New Baneshwar, Kathmandu, counted from hospital reports.
verification_note: The Kathmandu Post and the Himalayan Times each reported 14 on the afternoon of 8 Sep; the count rose the same evening.

title: Death toll: 17 killed in Kathmandu on 8 Sep
statement: Seventeen people were killed in Kathmandu on 8 September 2025 (HimalPress, HRW, and the sum of INSEC's hospital counts), plus two outside the capital in Itahari.
figure_more: Plus 2 outside the capital, in Itahari
verification_note: The Ministry of Health, as quoted by Onlinekhabar on the evening of 8 Sep, said 16 were killed in Kathmandu. HimalPress, HRW and INSEC's hospital counts (3+8+3+2+1) give 17.

title: Death toll: 18 dead on the evening of 8 Sep
statement: By the evening of 8 September 2025 the death toll from the Gen Z protests had risen to 18, with 200 to 256 injured.
verification_note: The Himalayan Times and Onlinekhabar both reported 18 on 8 Sep; the figure was raised to 19 about two hours later.

title: Death toll: 19 killed on 8 Sep (as reported that night)
statement: At least 19 people were killed during the 8 September 2025 protests: 17 in Kathmandu and two in Itahari, as reported on the night of 8 Sep and the following day.
verification_note: Reported by the Kathmandu Post, Himalayan Times, Setopati, Reuters (via CBC), HRW, The Guardian and Al Jazeera. Later official figures give 20 or 21 for 8 Sep; see the separate claims.

title: Death toll: 20 died on 8 Sep (committee report, Dec 2025)
statement: According to the Prime Minister's Secretariat, 20 people died on 8 September 2025, 37 on 9 September and 20 more in the following days, a total of 77.
figure_more: 37 on 9 September and 20 more in the following days, total 77
verification_note: Conflicts with 21 for 8 Sep (ANI, 16 Sep; Hamro Patro) and with the 19 reported at the time. The breakdown 20/37/20 also differs from ANI's 21/39/12 (a total of 72 on 16 Sep).

title: Death toll: 21 died on 8 Sep
statement: Twenty-one people died on 8 September 2025: ANI (16 Sep) says 21 protesters, all under 30, and a further 39 on 9 September and 12 over the next seven days; Hamro Patro (2026) also says police killed 21 on 8 Sep.
figure_more: 39 on 9 September and 12 over the next seven days
verification_note: Conflicts with 19 (reports of 8 Sep) and 20 (committee report, Dec 2025). ANI's day split (21/39/12) sums to 72; the committee's split (20/37/20) sums to 77.

title: Death toll: 30 (Ministry of Health, 10 Sep)
statement: The Ministry of Health and Population announced on the evening of 10 September 2025 that the death toll from the 8 September protest and its aftermath was 30.
verification_note: ANI report only; the Ministry release itself was not retrieved.

title: Death toll: 31 in the Kathmandu Valley (11 Sep)
statement: The death toll in the Kathmandu Valley reached 31 by 11 September 2025, according to the forensic department at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital as reported by The Kathmandu Post.
verification_note: ANI relaying The Kathmandu Post; the Post article itself was not retrieved. Counts Kathmandu Valley only.

title: Death toll: 51 (12-13 Sep)
statement: By 12 to 13 September 2025, 51 people had died in the protests and unrest, per the Ministry of Health and Population and police.
verification_note: ANI, Al Jazeera and DW agree on 51; Al Jazeera and DW cite the police spokesperson (AFP), so the police origin is one.

title: Death toll: 59 to nearly 60 (Republica, 14 Sep)
statement: Republica reported on 14 September 2025 that 59 had died, rising to almost 60 after two protesters with head gunshot wounds died at Bir Hospital.
figure_more: almost 60 after two protesters with head gunshot wounds died at Bir Hospital
verification_note: Republica only; the same day the Chief Secretary gave 72.

title: Death toll: 72 (Chief Secretary, 14 Sep)
statement: On 14 September 2025 Chief Secretary Eknarayan Aryal gave the death toll as 72: 59 protesters, 10 prison inmates and three security personnel.
verification_note: Onlinekhabar, The Himalayan Times and Ada Derana (citing local media) agree on 72 and the 59/10/3 split. Republica's count the same day was lower (59 to 60).

title: Death toll 72 to 74 by 14-21 September
statement: By 14 September Al Jazeera reported at least 72 killed; on 21 September The Kathmandu Post gave 74.
verification_note: Counts rose as injured people died, and sources use different counting dates. First-day toll is also given as 19 (Post) and 21 protesters (ANI, Al Jazeera). Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'confirmed': The claim records a toll rising with the counting date.

title: Death toll: 73 (confirmed by 17 Sep)
statement: The confirmed death toll stood at 73 before the Koteshwor Bhatbhateni body was found on 17 September 2025.
verification_note: Both Onlinekhabar and Republica give 73 as the figure before the 74th.

title: Death toll: 74 (17 Sep)
statement: After a charred body was found at the Koteshwor Bhatbhateni on 17 September 2025 the confirmed death toll reached 74; The Kathmandu Post on 19 Sep also says at least 74 and over 1,800 injured.
verification_note: Onlinekhabar, Republica and The Kathmandu Post agree.

title: Death toll: 75 (photo agency caption, about October 2025)
statement: A SOPA Images gallery published about a month after the protests says the protests 'left 75 people dead'.
verification_note: A photo caption only; no count source given. The date is approximate (the page gives none).

title: Death toll: 76 (Nov 2025)
statement: At least 76 people died during and in the days following the 8 and 9 September 2025 protests (Kathmandu Post, 4 Nov; HRW, 20 Nov).
verification_note: The Cabinet martyr decision named 45 of the 76; the Post says some charred bodies could not be identified. The committee report of 11 Dec gives 77.

title: At least 76 people killed on 8-9 September
statement: At least 76 people were killed in the 8-9 September 2025 protests and their aftermath.
verification_note: 76 is used by HRW (Feb 2026), the Kathmandu Post (Nov 2025), Reuters (Mar 2026), Setopati and others; 77 is used by IANS, the Kathmandu Post's report-leak coverage as summarised, and a search summary. Earlier tolls (72 on 14 Sep 2025, 51 on 12 Sep 2025) are on other agents' claims.

title: Death toll: 77 (committee report, 11 Dec 2025)
statement: A government committee headed by National Planning Commission secretary Ravilal Pantha reported 77 deaths and 2,429 injured, per the Prime Minister's Secretariat as reported by IANS; Hamro Patro (Sep 2026) also gives 77.
verification_note: 76 in the Kathmandu Post (4 Nov) and HRW (20 Nov), 75 in a SOPA caption. No source explains the difference.

title: 77 people killed on 8-9 September
statement: 77 people died over the two days of protests.
verification_note: Used by IANS (9 Sep 2026) and, per summaries, the Kathmandu Post's coverage of the leaked report. No verbatim anchor was available.

title: At least 51 killed by 12 September
statement: Police said on Friday 12 September that at least 51 people, including 21 protesters, nine prisoners and three police officers, had been killed since Monday.
verification_note: AP, AFP, Al Jazeera and Deccan Chronicle report the same police figure; AP and AFP may share wire origin.

title: Death toll reported on 11 September: 30 to 34
statement: On 11 September reports gave the protest death toll as 30 (Ada Derana), 31 (Al Jazeera, local media) and 34 (The Tribune, citing the health ministry).
figure_more: 31 (Al Jazeera, local media); 34 (The Tribune, citing the health ministry)
verification_note: Different tallies and counting times; superseded by the police figure of at least 51 on 12 September. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'confirmed': The claim records tallies taken at different times of one day.

title: Curfews and a protester death before 8 September
statement: RealShePower says curfews were imposed in Kathmandu Valley by 6 September and that a 19-year-old student was shot dead near Singha Durbar on 7 September. Other sources put the first deaths on 8 September.
verification_note: The Kathmandu District Security Committee found the situation normal on 7 September; HRW, Kathmandu Post and others date the killings to 8 September. No other source reports a death on 7 September.

title: The Budhanilkantha residence of Sher Bahadur Deuba was set on fire on 9 September 2025
statement: The Budhanilkantha residence of Sher Bahadur Deuba was set on fire on 9 September 2025.
verification_note: PTI and Setopati's attack report say the house was set on fire; Business Today says vehicles in the compound were burned; Setopati's other report says the home was vandalised, and Himal Press mentions looting inside without saying the house burned.

title: Inmates escaped from Dillibazar Jail (Republica photo report)
statement: Republica reported inmates escaped from Dillibazar Prison on Tuesday after breaking the Nepali Army cordon at the gate.
verification_note: Another Republica report says no inmates managed to flee Dillibazar's Charkhal Prison.

title: No inmates escaped from Dillibazar Jail (Republica)
statement: Republica reported that no inmates managed to flee from Dillibazar's Charkhal Prison, where hundreds staged demonstrations until late Wednesday night under the close watch of the Nepali Army.
verification_note: Contradicts the Republica photo report of 10 September and Khaleej Times describing inmates held back at the gate.

title: Attendance figures for the Discord debate on an interim leader
statement: More than 10,000 people joined the Youth Against Corruption Discord channel to debate an interim leader, and about 6,000 more watched a mirrored YouTube livestream.
verification_note: Al Jazeera (15 September) gives more than 10,000 in the channel plus about 6,000 on YouTube. Decode (24 September) quotes one participant's recollection of about 30,000 to 35,000 people listening to the main call. The Kathmandu Post (29 September) counts 7,713 votes in the open poll and notes there is no official platform data to verify participation and that anonymity may have allowed repeat voting. These measure different things (channel members, listeners, votes). Timing of the debate is reported inconsistently across sources: Al Jazeera places it on Thursday (11 September).

title: Discord poll result: Karki 3,833 of 7,713 votes
statement: In the open Discord poll Karki received 3,833 of 7,713 votes (about 50 percent). Wikipedia's table lists Rastra Bimochan Timalsena second (2,022, 26.22%), Sagar Dhakal third (1,098), then Harka Sampang and Mahabir Pun.
verification_note: Totals appear in the Kathmandu Post and, with a candidate table citing ClickMandu and Al Jazeera, in Wikipedia. No platform data were published. Wikipedia and Al Jazeera put participation in the debate itself above 10,000 people, which is a different measure.

title: Discord poll runner-up was Balen Shah (28%)
statement: An online poll organised by Gen Z activists on Wednesday had Karki on 50 per cent, followed by Kathmandu Mayor Balen Shah on 28 per cent, then Harka Sampang and Kulman Ghising.
verification_note: Contradicted by Al Jazeera and Wikipedia: the five-name shortlist was Sampang, Pun, Dhakal, Timalsina and Karki, Shah could not be reached by the moderators, and Timalsena is second in the Wikipedia table.

title: Discord vote cannot be independently verified
statement: Because Discord voting was anonymous, individuals might have voted more than once, and no official data from the platform exist to verify genuine participation.
verification_note: The Kathmandu Post and Al Jazeera, citing different participants and a journalist, make the same point independently. It is an assessment, not evidence of manipulation.

title: Discord was among the blocked platforms
statement: Discord was on the list of blocked platforms, so organisers used a blocked service. The Kathmandu Post and the Guardian lists do not mention it.
verification_note: Stated by heise, Swarajya, Green European Journal and Onlinekhabar. The Kathmandu Post list names only seven platforms as registered or pending. No outlet says Discord was left unblocked. Discord stayed usable through VPNs, per Green European Journal.

title: Dissolution demanded before the oath, carried out after it
statement: Youth delegates and Karki demanded that parliament be dissolved before the caretaker prime minister was appointed, while the President argued dissolution would follow once the new council of ministers announced elections. Other reports say Karki was sworn in first and parliament was dissolved at 11 pm on her government's recommendation.
verification_note: Nepali Times describes the order as the sticking point. Deccan Chronicle, ANI and The Kathmandu Post describe dissolution after the oath, on the prime minister's recommendation. Border Lens said the decree was drafted alongside the appointment letter.

title: Dissolution of the House of Representatives is unconstitutional
statement: The Nepali Congress, CPN-UML and CPN (Maoist Centre), and later eight parties jointly, said the President's dissolution of the House of Representatives on 12 September 2025 was unconstitutional. A commentator in The Wire describes the dissolution as applied under a doctrine of necessity that only partially wounded parliamentary democracy; President Paudel said on 14 September that the constitution had been saved.
verification_note: Parties' position is on record on 13-14 September; ten writs were filed at the Supreme Court by 15 October. The Wire (19 September) argues the opposite. No court ruling was retrieved.

title: Early deaths from rubber bullets
statement: The first deaths were caused by rubber bullets.
verification_note: Onlinekhabar's interim reports said the dead suffered critical injuries from rubber bullets. HRW and Amnesty later documented live ammunition; HRW says shots hit head, chest and abdomen with military rifles.

title: Education minister resigned for health reasons
statement: Education Minister Bidya Bhattarai resigned because of health issues; she had surgery on her neck.
verification_note: The same article reports differences with the PM and finance minister over teachers' demands as the actual reason.

title: Education minister resigned over a rift on teachers' demands
statement: Bidya Bhattarai resigned after the prime minister and the finance minister refused to fund teachers' salary and benefit demands, estimated at Rs150-200 billion a year.
verification_note: Rift is the Kathmandu Post's reporting; the retrieved text did not give a named source for the cost estimate.

title: Expected turnout was about 8,000
statement: The Valley Operations Division assessed around 8,000 protesters could attend. Others gave 6,000 to 7,000 (Oli), 3,500 to 5,000 (NID chief) and 3,000 to 5,000 (Kathmandu SSP). An NHRC-reported figure says the rally began with 3,000 to 3,200 and swelled to 20,000 to 25,000.
verification_note: All pre-protest estimates come from testimony to the Karki Commission as reported by Onlinekhabar. Deployment figures also differ: 3,441 plus 505 police vs 4,396.

title: Finance Minister Bishnu Prasad Paudel was stripped of his clothes and pushed into a river...
statement: Finance Minister Bishnu Prasad Paudel was stripped of his clothes and pushed into a river by protesters on 9 September 2025.
verification_note: Gulf News describes video showing this. TBS describes him chased on foot and beaten and does not mention a river. Not confirmed by a second retrievable source.

title: More than seven petitions against dissolution on the first day
statement: On the first day of registrations after the arson, more than seven writ petitions against dissolution of the House were received (14 October 2025).
verification_note: Conflicts with the Kathmandu Post's 14 petitions received on 15 October.

title: First shots at 12 37
statement: Police opened fire for the first time at 12:37 pm, at protesters who had climbed onto a small building near the Parliament gate.
verification_note: Harvard timeline. The Kathmandu Post puts the start of gunfire just before 1 pm; the BBC (via Ratopati) puts the radio order at 12:40 pm; HRW gives a window from about 12:30 pm.

title: FNJ: 26 press freedom incidents on the protest days
statement: During the 23 Bhadra (8 September) protests there were 26 press freedom violation incidents affecting more than 100 journalists and media institutions (FNJ).
figure_more: more than 100 journalists and media institutions affected
verification_note: FNJ covers a wider category (including property damage) than CPJ or RSF. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': FNJ counts a wider category than CPJ or RSF; a difference of definition.

title: Former King Gyanendra met the protesters
statement: A claim circulated that former King Gyanendra had met the protesters. Gen Z organisers found that an old video of him interacting with youngsters was being shared.
verification_note: Debunked by the Gen Z fact-check room as reported by Al Jazeera; Nepali Times separately reports widespread rumours of a Gyanendra comeback bid on 11 September.

title: Gen Z groups did not agree on Karki
statement: On 10-11 September different groups claiming to represent Gen Z backed different interim leaders (Karki, Balen Shah, Harka Sampang); supporters of Shah and Sampang said they would not accept Karki.
verification_note: Reported by Setopati, Ada Derana, Al Jazeera and Nepali Times independently.

title: Indian TV claim that the Gen Z protest was a CIA plot
statement: Republic TV said on air that the Nepal protest was 'a pure CIA plot'.
verification_note: Reported by Newslaundry (9 September 2025), which criticises the foreign-hand claims as an attempt to shift the story from Nepal's governance crisis to a geopolitical thriller. No source retrieved offers evidence for the claim.

title: Claim that the Gen Z protests were a demand for a Hindu state or monarchy
statement: Posts and broadcasts in India described the September 2025 protests as a movement demanding a Hindu nation (Hindu Rashtra) or the restoration of the monarchy.
verification_note: Assessment: false or baseless. AFP says old footage of protesters calling for a Hindu monarchy was falsely shared as evidence. IPS, The Diplomat Nepal and The Quint reach the same finding. Related: claim:sikkim-rally-video-shown-as-nepali-protesters-for-hindu-rashtra-or-modi.

title: Officials say this is registration, not a ban
statement: Officials, including Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba on 6 September, say the government is not closing social media but requiring registration. Critics and several outlets call it a blanket ban.
verification_note: Characterisation conflict: BBC, Kantipur and Setopati report the government view; Kathmandu Post and the Guardian describe a ban or blanket ban.

title: Government account: casualties occurred as the Special Task Force blocked entry to a vital installation
statement: Those in power said the casualties on 8 September 2025 occurred when the Special Task Force of the Nepal Police tried to prevent protesters from entering a sensitive area or vital installation.
verification_note: Onlinekhabar (8 September 2026) says Oli and other leaders, officials and security personnel repeated this before the inquiry commission and in court responses. Human-rights activists describe disproportionate and unusually lethal use of force, and the commission concluded that the use of guns and metal bullets was a mistake on the government's side.

title: Gunfire began just before 1pm
statement: Gunfire began just before 1 pm, from inside Parliament.
verification_note: Kathmandu Post narrative. Harvard says 12:37 pm; BBC (via Ratopati) says the order was at 12:40 pm.

title: Probe committee cleared Gurung
statement: A committee examining Gurung's assets and shares concluded the allegations could not be substantiated.
verification_note: Reported by ShareSansar, Kathmandu Post and IANS on the day of reappointment.

title: Hami Nepal obtained the district administration’s permission
statement: Al Jazeera and India Today say Hami Nepal had obtained approval from the Kathmandu district administration. Onlinekhabar says two individuals went to the office on 7 September to seek permission, and the NID report says a Gen Z group asked for security arrangements.
verification_note: Three different requesters are named. The district administration’s own record was not retrieved.

title: Hami Nepal organised the 8 September protest
statement: Al Jazeera, India Today and Nepali Times describe Hami Nepal as an organiser or key coordinator. BBC, Onlinekhabar and Gurung himself say there was no single organiser or that he did not start the movement.
verification_note: Onlinekhabar found that several people later seen as Gen Z leaders did not know who called the protest. Hami Nepal’s own 7 September post says it was only there to guide and keep people safe. The logistics role (tents, ambulances, sound) is not disputed in the NHRC report.

title: Indian TV claim that Hami Nepal received Rs 20 crore from Coca-Cola and Viber
statement: Aaj Tak said an NGO called 'Ham Nepal' received Rs 20 crore in financial support from Coca-Cola, Viber and other companies to organise the violent protests.
verification_note: Reported and criticised by Newslaundry (9 September 2025). No source retrieved supports the funding claim.

title: Hilton Kathmandu damage of about NPR 8 billion
statement: INSEC reports the Hilton Hotel in Kathmandu alone suffered around NPR 8 billion of damage; AFP puts the damage at about $56 million.
verification_note: The NPR and dollar figures are consistent. The Oriental Insurance Company reported NPR 5.14 billion in claims, much of it attributed to the Hilton.

title: Hilton Kathmandu set on fire
statement: Agitators set fire to the Hilton Hotel in Kathmandu on 9 September.
verification_note: Single report of 9 Sept.

title: Home Minister says the arrest is not revenge
statement: Home Minister Sudan Gurung said the arrests were not an act of revenge but the beginning of bringing those responsible for suppressing the protests to justice.
verification_note: Opposed by Oli's claim of retaliation.

title: Hospital split 8 3 3 2 1
statement: Of 17 dead in Kathmandu hospitals: 8 at the National Trauma Centre, 3 at Everest Hospital, 3 at Civil Hospital, 2 at Kathmandu Medical College and 1 at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.
figure_more: 8 National Trauma Centre; 3 Everest Hospital; 3 Civil Hospital; 2 Kathmandu Medical College; 1 Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital
verification_note: Kathmandu Post and ANI/Tribune agree with each other, and HRW says the Trauma Centre received 8; Himal Press gives a different split (see hospital-split-himalpress-6-5-3-2-1).

title: Hospital split himalpress 6 5 3 2 1
statement: Of 17 dead: Civil Hospital 3, National Trauma Center 6, Kathmandu Medical College 2, Everest Hospital 5, TU Teaching Hospital 1.
figure_more: 6 National Trauma Centre; 5 Everest Hospital; 3 Civil Hospital; 2 Kathmandu Medical College; 1 Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital
verification_note: Himal Press's split sums to 17 but differs from the Kathmandu Post/ANI split on the Trauma Centre (6 vs 8) and Everest (5 vs 3). The page excerpt retrieved gives the numbers in text that could not be quoted verbatim, so no anchor is attached.

title: Viral video: police officer's house torched in Chitwan
statement: A video was shared claiming a police officer's house was torched in Chitwan after a traffic police fine of Rs 25,000.
verification_note: Newschecker says it shows an arson attack on a police station in Banepa during the 9 September protests.

title: HRW: 35 of 47 bodies at one Kathmandu morgue had high-velocity gunshot wounds
statement: Pathologists at a Kathmandu morgue that received 47 bodies over the two days told HRW that 35 deaths were due to high-velocity gunshot wounds to the head, neck, chest or abdomen.
scope: Kathmandu morgue (47 bodies received over the two days)
verification_note: HRW's interviews with pathologists; no second source for the 47 and 35.

title: Indonesian video shown as Nepali protesters attacking police
statement: A video of police sheltering behind riot shields under attack was shared on 10 September 2025 as showing Nepali protesters attacking police.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Alt News traced the video to protests in Indonesia in late August 2025; The Quint's weekly recap reports the same finding. Alt News says the national editor of the Hindi daily Dainik Bhaskar was among those who shared it.

title: CPN-UML claim that infiltrators turned the peaceful protest violent
statement: CPN-UML said that criminal groups infiltrated a peaceful youth protest on 9 September 2025 and turned it violent, using young protesters as human shields and encouraging the attack on Parliament.
verification_note: CPN-UML's 2026 statement and an Onlinekhabar opinion piece (12 September 2025) support the infiltration account. The investigation commission, as reported by Onlinekhabar, said attacks on state structures cannot be confined to being merely impulsive, but it also found the use of guns and metal bullets was a mistake on the government's side. Balendra Shah, then Kathmandu mayor, said the 9 September incident was triggered by the government's excessive, terrorist-style use of force on 8 September.

title: 2,660 verified injured
statement: The government's finalised list of verified injured from the Gen Z movement stands at 2,660 (1 May 2026).
verification_note: Differs from the 2,522 wounded that Reuters attributes to the commission report; the two may count different things (verified list against report tally). Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': A finalised list of May 2026 after the March 2026 report tally; an update.

title: Injured 347
statement: At least 347 injured protesters were being treated in hospitals nationwide.
verification_note: Kathmandu Post, ShareSansar and All India Radio give 347; Onlinekhabar, Kathmandu Post's resignation article and INSEC give more than 400; HRW and Amnesty give over 300; Al Jazeera's gallery caption says more than 100.

title: Injured more than 100
statement: More than 100 people were injured.
verification_note: Al Jazeera gallery caption; an early or conservative figure compared with 347 and 400+.

title: Injured: over 100 (Amnesty, 8 Sep)
statement: Amnesty International reported on 8 September 2025 'over 100 injured' alongside at least 19 dead.
verification_note: Same-day counts differ by hour and source: 100+ (Amnesty), 145 (Reuters), 256 (Onlinekhabar), over 300 (HRW), 347 (Ministry of Health), 453 (INSEC, 9 Sep). Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': Same-day counts differ by hour and source; they form a running count.

title: Injured: 1,033 recorded (Ministry of Health, 10 Sep)
statement: The Ministry of Health and Population said on 10 September 2025 that 1,033 injuries had been recorded nationwide, 713 of the injured already discharged.
verification_note: ANI relaying the Ministry release.

title: Injured: more than 1,300 (Al Jazeera, 12 Sep)
statement: Al Jazeera reported on 12 September 2025 that the week's protests had injured more than 1,300 people.
verification_note: No second source in this set for 1,300; the Ministry gave 1,033 two days earlier.

title: Injured: 145 including 28 officers (Reuters, 8 Sep)
statement: At least 145 people were wounded on 8 September 2025, including 28 officers, officials told Reuters.
verification_note: Earlier snapshot than 256 and 347 the same evening; see the injury claims for 8-9 Sep.

title: Injured: over 1,800 (Kathmandu Post, 19 Sep)
statement: The Kathmandu Post wrote on 19 September 2025 that over 1,800 people had been injured, and 196 were still under care at 32 hospitals.
verification_note: Post figure, from the Health Emergency Operation Centre data it cites for the 196.

title: Injured: nearly 2,000 on 8 Sep (Hamro Patro, 2026)
statement: A Hamro Patro article of 11 September 2026 says police fire on 8 September 2025 killed 21 and injured nearly 2,000.
verification_note: Day-one counts at the time were 145 to 453; 2,429 is the total for 8-9 Sep across the country in the committee report. The 'nearly 2,000' is attributed to 8 Sep alone.

title: Injured: 2,429 (committee report, 11 Dec 2025)
statement: A government committee reported 2,429 injured in the nationwide protests, of whom 17 were under 13 years old and 1,433 between 13 and 28 (IANS, 11 Dec 2025).
verification_note: IANS relaying the committee report; the report itself was not retrieved.

title: Injured: 256 (Ministry of Health via Onlinekhabar, 8 Sep)
statement: At least 256 people were injured on 8 September 2025, per the Ministry of Health as cited by Onlinekhabar.
verification_note: Differs from 145, 347 and 453 on the same day.

title: Injured: over 300 (HRW, Himalayan Times, 8-9 Sep)
statement: More than 300 people were injured on 8 September 2025 (HRW 9 Sep; Himalayan Times headline 8 Sep).
verification_note: Differs from 145, 256, 347 and 453 on the same day.

title: Injured: 347 (Ministry of Health and Population, 8 Sep)
statement: The Ministry of Health and Population counted 347 injured nationwide on the evening of 8 September 2025.
verification_note: Differs from 256 (Onlinekhabar, same evening) and 453 (INSEC).

title: Injured: over 453 (INSEC, 9 Sep)
statement: INSEC reported on 9 September 2025 that over 453 people were injured in the 8 September protests, listing hospital counts.
verification_note: Higher than the Ministry's 347 of the previous evening; hospital snapshots differ.

title: NPR 20.7 billion in insurance claims by 16 September
statement: The Nepal Insurance Authority reported non-life insurers received 1,984 claims worth NPR 20.7 billion by 16 September, above the NPR 16.5 billion claimed after the 2015 earthquake.
verification_note: INSEC later reports claims of NPR 22.2565 billion; the figures are from different dates. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': Claims by 16 September, later 22.26 billion; different dates.

title: NPR 22.26 billion in insurance claims (INSEC, 24 Sept)
statement: INSEC reports the Nepal Insurance Authority said claims for damage from the protests reached Rs 22,256,500,000, with Bagmati Province accounting for Rs 17,977,200,000.
verification_note: Later than the 20.7 billion figure; not necessarily a contradiction. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': Claims by 24 September, after the 20.7 billion of 16 September; different dates.

title: Itahari police fired after stones at police office
statement: Police in Itahari opened fire after protesters threw stones at the Area Police Office, following arrests of youths involved in arson.
verification_note: Republica says police fired after stone-pelting at the Area Police Office after arrests for arson; Himal Press says police fired after demonstrators marched to the Area Police Office following arson; Himalayan Times does not give a cause.

title: Joint statement signed by nine missions
statement: The 9 September joint statement was signed by nine missions: Australia, Finland, France, Japan, South Korea, the United Kingdom, the United States, Germany and Norway (Diplomat Nepal).
verification_note: B360 Nepal lists seven, without Germany and Norway.

title: Joint statement signed by seven missions
statement: The 9 September joint statement was signed by Australia, Finland, France, Japan, South Korea, the United Kingdom and the United States (B360 Nepal).
verification_note: Diplomat Nepal lists nine, adding Germany and Norway.

title: Kantipur building fire reported 12:50 GMT
statement: Al Jazeera's live blog reported at 12:50 GMT (18:35 Nepal time) that protesters set fire to a building housing Kantipur Publications.
verification_note: Posting time of a live-blog entry; the gap with HRW's 13:30 to 14:00 may be lag or a second attack.

title: Kantipur TV attacked 13:30 to 14:00
statement: Men with sticks, knives and gasoline vandalised Kantipur Television's headquarters between 1:30 and 2 p.m. on 9 September.
verification_note: Conflicts with the Al Jazeera live-blog stamp (12:50 GMT = 18:35 Nepal time) for the fire at the Kantipur building.

title: Karki ineligible: non-member of the House and former chief justice
statement: Petitioners argue the appointment of Karki breaches Article 76 (a prime minister must be a member of the lower house) and Article 132 (a former chief justice is not eligible for appointment to any government office). IANS reported on 13 September that she was appointed under the "principle of necessity".
verification_note: Argued in writs filed at the Supreme Court (Kathmandu Post, 15 Oct); the question was flagged on 12-13 September by Al Jazeera and IANS. No ruling was retrieved.

title: Karki was chosen through a Discord poll
statement: Sushila Karki was chosen as interim prime minister through a public vote held by Gen Z leaders on Discord. Participants quoted by the Kathmandu Post call "the PM was chosen only through Discord" an overstatement: the army facilitated an agreement with the President and Karki also had support beyond youth circles.
verification_note: Agency copy (ANI) and Al Jazeera present the Discord poll as the selection mechanism; The Kathmandu Post (Asia News Network repost) quotes Gen Z participants rejecting that framing, and its army reconstruction says the army facilitated the agreement with the President.

title: The Kathmandu Post offices were set on fire
statement: RSF lists The Kathmandu Post among outlets whose offices were set on fire on 9 September.
verification_note: CPJ names only Kantipur Media Group and Annapurna Post as set on fire; the Kantipur and Kathmandu Post websites went down.

title: Khapung and rijal deny issuing fire order
statement: Inspector General Chandra Kuber Khapung and the District Security Committee chief Chhabilal Rijal say they did not issue an order to fire.
verification_note: Denial as reported by Ratopati citing the BBC. Registry id person:chhabi-rijal is used for Chhabilal Rijal on the basis of the name only; the source does not give his office beyond 'District Security Committee chief'.

title: 1,280 inmates escaped from Lalitpur jail (INSEC)
statement: INSEC reported 1,280 inmates escaped from the Lalitpur jail.
verification_note: Assumed to be Nakkhu, which is in Lalitpur, but INSEC's page as retrieved does not name Nakkhu.

title: Lamichhane charges are politically motivated
statement: Supporters of Rabi Lamichhane said the charges against him were politically motivated.
verification_note: Opposed by the findings of a parliamentary committee, which concluded the evidence did not show him innocent.

title: Lamichhane left Nakkhu on a counterfeit letter
statement: Republica reported Lamichhane left Nakkhu by presenting a counterfeited letter from the prison management, and that management was forced to let him go after hundreds of supporters pressed the outnumbered guards.
verification_note: Onlinekhabar's 9 September report says police handed him to his wife after they could no longer provide security. Lamichhane maintains the letter was genuine.

title: Lamichhane's release letter was issued through due process
statement: Rabi Lamichhane claimed he was released through due process and made public a release letter signed by Prison Administrator Satyaraj Joshi.
verification_note: Republica says Joshi later declined to take ownership of the letter and calls it counterfeit.

title: Lekhak did not order police to fire
statement: Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak said he did not order police to open fire and had told them to use water cannon and batons only.
verification_note: Statement quoted by Himal Press as he announced his resignation. No independent record of his instructions was found.

title: Lethal force between 12 30 and 4pm
statement: Police used lethal force between around 12:30 and 4 pm.
verification_note: HRW's reconstruction from video and interviews; consistent with, and wider than, the Harvard and Kathmandu Post start times.

title: Major business enterprises report over NPR 60 billion (CNI official)
statement: IANS quotes a Confederation of Nepalese Industries official saying major business enterprises alone reported damages worth over NPR 60 billion.
verification_note: One source retrieved.

title: Video of a slingshot attack on 'Malacañang Palace' shows Nepal's Parliament
statement: A video showing a masked protester shooting at Malacañang Palace in the Philippines with a slingshot was widely shared.
verification_note: Assessment: false. VERA Files says the footage was taken in front of Nepal's Parliament Building. The original Facebook post, with more than 10 million views, had been taken down by the time of the fact-check. Single fact-checker.

title: Cabinet declares 45 of the dead martyrs (3 Nov 2025)
statement: On 3 November 2025 the Cabinet, on a Home Ministry study, declared 45 people who died in the protests of 8 and 9 September 2025 martyrs; further studies on more cases were to follow.
figure_more: further studies on more cases were to follow
verification_note: HimalPress, INSEC and The Kathmandu Post agree on the decision and the number 45.

title: RSF: more than a dozen media outlets attacked on 9 September
statement: More than a dozen media outlets and three journalists' organisations were attacked on 9 September (RSF).
verification_note: Scale differs from CPJ (offices of two outlets set on fire) and FNJ (26 incidents affecting over 100 journalists and institutions); definitions of "attacked" differ. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': RSF, CPJ and FNJ count different things; a difference of definition.

title: More than 3,300 prisoners escaped from Nakkhu (Republica)
statement: Republica reported more than 3,300 prisoners escaped from Nakkhu Prison.
verification_note: INSEC lists a Lalitpur jail figure of 1,280.

title: Names of the five registered platforms differ
statement: Five platforms had registered by the deadline: TikTok, Viber and three others. Outlets name the others as Witk, Nimbuzz and Popo Live (Kathmandu Post); Nimbuzz, WeTalk and Poppo Live (Himalayan Times); Nimbuzz, WeTalk and Opolite (Onlinekhabar). Telegram and a second platform ("Global Diary" or "GlobalLink") were in process.
verification_note: Spelling or transliteration differences are likely (Witk/WeTalk, Popo Live/Poppo Live/Opolite, Global Diary/GlobalLink); the ministry notice was not retrieved to settle them.

title: Naubasta: five juvenile inmates killed on the night of 9 Sep
statement: Police fire killed five juvenile inmates and seriously injured four at the Naubasta juvenile correctional home in Banke on the night of 9 September 2025.
verification_note: Both articles are ANI reports; the second cites The Kathmandu Post.

title: Nearly 900 inmates escaped from two western prisons
statement: Two prisons in western Nepal were stormed, with nearly 900 inmates escaping.
verification_note: Fox News summary of 9 Sept; early figure for two prisons only, so it may not conflict with the larger national count.

title: Nepal Gen Z footage shared as a student protest in Chhattisgarh
statement: In June 2026 a video of police using water cannon was shared on Instagram as students protesting over government job vacancies in Chhattisgarh, India.
verification_note: Assessment: misleading. Fact Crescendo found the video originated from the September 2025 Gen Z protests in Nepal. Later reuse of the footage, outside the protest period.

title: Nepo-kid campaign was gaining traction when the ban came
statement: The social media ban came just as a viral online movement targeting political elites and their children was gaining traction.
verification_note: Conflicts with Global Voices, which says the trend emerged after the ban announcement.

title: Nepo-kid trend emerged after the ban announcement
statement: The nepo-kid trend emerged following the social media ban announcement, with campaigns pairing 'nepotism' with 'kid'.
verification_note: Global Voices text retrieved paraphrased; no verbatim sentence.

title: NHRC blames Oli, Lekhak and Gurung for the 8-9 September violence
statement: NHRC explicitly blamed Oli, former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak and former Communications Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung for the street violence on 8 and 9 September.
verification_note: OCCRP report; HRW spells Lekhak "Lekakh". Himal Press confirms a report with findings on state failure and excessive force, but not the named ministers.

title: Ministry of Health death toll of 36 (12 September 2025)
statement: The Ministry of Health reported on 12 September 2025 that the death toll from the protests had reached 36, with 1,760 injured nationwide, based on hospital data.
verification_note: Later counts are higher: 72 (Chief Secretary, 14 September) and 74 (Kathmandu police, 17 September). The 36 is a hospital-based count at one date, so it differs from later cumulative counts that include prisoners and security personnel.

title: Claim that Oli died after an accident (October 2024)
statement: A TikTok post in October 2024 claimed Prime Minister Oli had been in an accident and died during treatment.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal found a press report (dated 4 Kartik 2081, about 20 October 2024) of Oli attending a CPN-UML secretariat meeting, and quoted his press coordinator as saying he was safe.

title: Oli and Lekhak arrested on 27 March
statement: The Himalayan Times says Oli and Lekhak were arrested on 27 March 2026.
verification_note: The Tribune, Jurist and others say early Saturday 28 March; the Himalayan Times item is a passing reference.

title: Oli and Lekhak arrested on 28 March
statement: Oli and Lekhak were arrested early on Saturday 28 March 2026.
verification_note: Conflicts with the Himalayan Times's 27 March.

title: Oli and CPN-UML: the uprising was a foreign conspiracy or planned plot
statement: KP Sharma Oli dismissed the deaths of young protesters as a foreign conspiracy and an attempt to burn the country, and CPN-UML described 8 and 9 September as a dangerous plan to push the country into authoritarianism, anarchy and geopolitical conflict.
verification_note: Oli's words come from an Onlinekhabar opinion piece (7 March 2026), not a direct transcript. The UML statement (9 September 2026) names no group or country. No source retrieved provides evidence of foreign involvement.

title: Claim that Oli had been arrested (October 2025)
statement: TikTok posts from 23 October 2025 suggested that former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli had been arrested.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal found no authority had ordered his arrest. The posts reused video of Prime Minister Karki leaving Shital Niwas after her oath on 12 September 2025.

title: Oli: violence caused by "vested interest groups"
statement: Prime Minister Oli said he was saddened by the violence and blamed "vested interest groups" (HRW).
verification_note: HRW report of Oli's statement; no primary text retrieved. Related to the claim that Oli told cabinet the protest was infiltrated.

title: Claim that Oli was convicted by an international court of crimes against humanity
statement: A TikTok video claimed that an international court had convicted former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli of crimes against humanity and sentenced him to death.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal says the video used a photo of a retired U.S. municipal judge who is well known online. Published 13 December 2025.

title: Condolence posts claiming Oli had died (January 2025)
statement: TikTok posts on 27 and 28 January 2025 offered condolences for Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli, claiming he had died.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal says Oli had only common cold symptoms and carried out official functions in person and virtually.

title: Claim that former PM Oli had died of a heart attack (video of 23 September 2025)
statement: A TikTok video posted on 23 September 2025 carried the text 'Heartfelt condolence. Former Prime Minister KP Oli is no more.'
verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal states that Oli was alive. At the time he had been flown to an army barrack after resigning on 9 September and later moved to a rented apartment in Bhaktapur.

title: Claim that Oli was the first and only Nepali PM never to visit India in office
statement: On 9 September 2025 a journalist at WION and other social media users said KP Sharma Oli was the first and only Nepali prime minister who never visited India during his term.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Alt News and The Quint say Oli visited India as prime minister in 2016 and 2018. Alt News adds that the journalist later clarified in a thread that Oli had not visited during his third term.

title: Oli fled the country after resigning
statement: Multiple reports on 9 September claimed that KP Sharma Oli had fled the country. Oli wrote on 10 September that he was at the Shivapuri barracks and had not left Nepal; Setopati and The Tribune also place him under army protection at Shivapuri.
verification_note: Contradicted by Oli's own letter and two outlets. The Kathmandu Post (30 Sept) says Oli left the PM residence in an army helicopter, which is consistent with leaving the residence, not the country.

title: Oli left Nepal after resigning on 9 September 2025
statement: Oli left Nepal after resigning on 9 September 2025.
verification_note: Daily Guardian says multiple reports on Tuesday claimed Oli had fled the country. Oli later said he was at the Shivapuri barracks and had not left. Setopati reports he was flown by army helicopter to the Army Command and Staff College at Shivapuri.

title: Video said to show a new Oli interview after Sushila Karki became interim PM
statement: A TikTok video was shared as a fresh interview of KP Sharma Oli after his resignation and the appointment of Sushila Karki as interim prime minister.
verification_note: Assessment: misleading. Newschecker Nepal matched the clip to an interview posted on 30 July 2016, after Oli's first resignation as prime minister.

title: Oli government's flood response was slow and under-prepared
statement: The Oli government was criticised for a slow response to the September 2024 floods and for a lack of preparedness for the monsoon season.
verification_note: Three independent publishers report the criticism; none retrieved carries a government rebuttal.

title: Claim that Oli had a heart attack and was taken to Grande Hospital (October 2024)
statement: A TikTok video posted on 2 October 2024 said Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli had suffered a heart attack and been taken to Grande Hospital.
verification_note: Assessment: misleading. Newschecker Nepal says the footage was from a November 2018 hospital visit combined with false text. Build-up period, before the 2025 protests.

title: Claim that Oli left a secret resignation letter blaming opposition to Ram's birthplace
statement: News18 and IBC24 claimed that former Prime Minister Oli had left behind a secret resignation letter blaming his ouster on opposition to Lord Ram's birthplace in Ayodhya.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Decode (BOOM) states that no such letter existed. Single source.

title: Oli's resignation letter states that he was appointed prime minister on Asar 31, 2071 BS u...
statement: Oli's resignation letter states that he was appointed prime minister on Asar 31, 2071 BS under Article 76(2).
verification_note: Himalayan Times quotes 'Asar 31, 2071 BS'. Himal Press and Setopati quote 'July 15, 2024'. Oli took office in July 2024, so the 2071 year in the Himalayan Times quote looks like an error, but the original letter was not seen.

title: Oli said protest was infiltrated
statement: Prime Minister Oli told the cabinet the peaceful demonstration had been infiltrated by disruptive elements.
verification_note: Paraphrase in the Kathmandu Post report via ANN; no direct Oli quote retrieved.

title: Oli says his arrest was retaliatory
statement: Oli said 'This arrest is retaliatory. I will fight it legally.'
verification_note: Oli's account is contradicted by Home Minister Gurung's statement that it is not revenge; the courts' orders (remand, then release on Supreme Court direction) are recorded as actions.

title: Oli says arson and attacks were premeditated
statement: Oli says infiltrators and conspirators created the violence, that the arson and attacks on all three organs of government were premeditated, and (9 Sep 2026) that the destruction was the result of a planned attempt to undermine democracy.
verification_note: Assertion by one claimant over several statements; no source retrieved tests it.

title: Oli: he did not order police to open fire; the prime minister does not order police
statement: In written statements to the Gauri Bahadur Karki-led inquiry panel and the National Human Rights Commission, Oli denied personal involvement in ordering police to open fire on the first day, and said the prime minister does not issue orders to the police.
