verification_note: The Kathmandu Post (5 January 2026) attributes the account to an official, not to a direct quote. Police told BBC Eye Investigations the force directive followed approval from the government security committee. The investigation commission recommended a criminal investigation against Oli, then Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak and then IGP Chandra Kuber Khapung, and said Oli's failure to prevent further loss of life was a major weakness. The commission did not, in the retrieved text, state that Oli gave a firing order.

title: Oli: no firing order given
statement: KP Sharma Oli said he neither gave an order to fire nor could think of giving one, and that no force was used at the Maitighar demonstration.
verification_note: Statement of 28 January 2026 as reported by Kantipur (Nepali). It does not address who else may have ordered force; the BBC reports an order from the IGP.

title: Oli: lost power over his stand on Ayodhya and the borders
statement: In a letter written from Shivapuri on 10 September, Oli said he lost power because he opposed the birth of Lord Ram in Ayodhya and insisted Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura belong to Nepal.
verification_note: Oli's own statement as reported by The Daily Guardian; no independent corroboration of the causal claim was retrieved.

title: After resigning, Oli was flown by army helicopter to the Army Command and Staff College at...
statement: After resigning, Oli was flown by army helicopter to the Army Command and Staff College at Shivapuri and stayed under army protection.
verification_note: Setopati (10 September) and Daily Guardian (11 September, citing Oli's own statement) agree on the Shivapuri location. Daily Guardian calls it the Shivapuri barracks.

title: One Indian national among the dead
statement: One Indian national, Rajesh Devi Gola of Ghaziabad, was among those who died, after a Kathmandu hotel was set on fire on 9 September 2025.
verification_note: The Nepal Police co-spokesperson (via ANI) and the Tribune's own report agree on one Indian national.

title: Order authorised by a security committee
statement: Police stated Khapung gave the order only after authorisation from a government security committee headed by a senior civil servant.
verification_note: Police statement as relayed by AFP (News24). Not independently verified here.

title: Security source: "orders from above" to respond aggressively
statement: A credible security source told HRW that there were orders from above to respond aggressively to the protests.
verification_note: HRW says it could not corroborate the source.

title: 2022 Pakistan video of tear gas canister being thrown back shown as Nepal
statement: A video of a young man catching a tear gas canister and throwing it back was shared on 22 September 2025 as viral in Nepal.
verification_note: Assessment: false. Alt News traced it to a Gulf Today Facebook video uploaded on 25 May 2022 from Pakistan.

title: The parliament building still stands (Sushila Karki)
statement: AFP quotes former Chief Justice Sushila Karki saying 'The parliament still stands.'
verification_note: Carnegie states the Parliament was incinerated, and Republica reports fires inside the building; reporting agrees it was set on fire but not on how much was destroyed.

title: Partial shutdown of Facebook, X and TikTok announced 5 September
statement: RealShePower says the government announced on 5 September a partial shutdown of platforms including Facebook, X and TikTok, effective 7 September. Mainstream sources say the order was on 4 September and TikTok was exempt.
verification_note: Contradicted by AP, Guardian and Kathmandu Post (order on 4 September, TikTok registered and not blocked).

title: Party cadres took part in the 9 September arson
statement: The commission found political party activists infiltrated the public outrage, with local leaders and cadres of several parties directly involved in arson on 9 September.
verification_note: Ratopati summary; the report text was not read.

title: Which festival and date the Pashupatinath gate video shows
statement: Fact-checkers give different accounts of when and during which festival the Pashupatinath Temple gate video was recorded: Naxal Bhagwati Jatra on 31 March 2025, Basleshwori Jatra at the end of March 2025, or the Vatsaleshwori Jatra about two months before 9 September.
verification_note: Newschecker gives 31 March 2025 and the Naxal Bhagwati Jatra. BOOM gives the second day of the Basleshwori Jatra, around the end of March 2025. Alt News and AFP also say Naxal Bhagwati Jatra. IPS, summarising a fact-check, says the clip was uploaded nearly two months earlier during the Vatsaleshwori Jatra. The three festival names and the two dates are not reconciled in the sources. All agree it was an older festival video and not a protest.

title: Peter one radio order 12 40
statement: A police radio message from 'Peter One' at 12:40 pm, attributed to an order from Inspector General Chandra Kuber Khapung, told units to use force; police then fired from the Parliament premises.
verification_note: Reported by Ratopati from a BBC investigation of radio logs and over 4,000 videos. The BBC article itself could not be fetched. Khapung and the District Security Committee chief deny giving such an order (see claim khapung-and-rijal-deny-issuing-fire-order). The home minister says he did not order firing (claim lekhak-did-not-order-police-to-fire). Harvard places the first shots at 12:37 pm, three minutes before the reported order.

title: Photos of a man from Darjeeling presented as the architect of the Gen Z movement
statement: Indian news channels News18 and Zee News published photos of a man from Darjeeling, claiming he was a key architect of the Gen Z movement, in a case of mistaken identity with the Hami Nepal coordinator.
verification_note: Source is a Darjeeling-based journalist quoted by IPS. IPS says the case nearly painted the movement as India-sponsored. The man's name is not used here.

title: Police compelled to fire after breach
statement: Security officials said police were compelled to open fire after protesters breached a restricted area and tried to enter Parliament.
verification_note: Himal Press attributes this to security officials. HRW says police fired directly at students and that lethal force was used between about 12:30 and 4 pm, and Amnesty says live fire was unlawful.

title: Police fired from inside the Parliament grounds
statement: Police fired at protesters from inside the Parliament compound, including officers about 40 m from the wall firing military rifles.
verification_note: HRW analysed a video; the BBC report (via Ratopati) says police fired from the premises; a protester told ANI gunfire could be heard from inside; AP says police sought safety inside the complex.

title: Live ammunition used on 8 September
statement: Police fired live ammunition at protesters on 8 September in Kathmandu.
verification_note: HRW, Amnesty and Reuters (forensics) agree; Reuters calls the forensic findings the first official confirmation.

title: Police personnel tell the commission shoot orders were given in the field
statement: Victim police personnel told the commission in a five-page application of 5 October 2025 that field commanders shouted orders to shoot immediately on 8 September, while a radio order the next day said under no circumstances to shoot or use force.
verification_note: Testimony as reported by the Himalayan Times; the named officers are not quoted in the retrieved text beyond the order wording. The commission later recommended departmental action against five police officers including two SSPs (Onlinekhabar).

title: Nepal Police: necessary force was ordered only after other forms of force were exhausted
statement: Nepal Police said the 8 September 2025 order to use necessary force was given only after approval from the government security committee and after all other forms of force permitted under Nepali law had been exhausted.
verification_note: The statement comes from Nepal Police as reported by BBC Eye Investigations (via Onlinekhabar, 26 February 2026). The same report cites a leaked police log in which 'Peter 1', identified by a source as former IGP Khapung, ordered 'use necessary force' ten minutes after the curfew began, and BBC video analysis of a minor who was unarmed and leaving the scene peacefully before he was killed. A human-rights activist told Onlinekhabar that police provoked protesters by firing tear gas and water cannon, and the investigation commission concluded the use of guns and metal bullets was a mistake on the government's side.

title: Prasai's arrested associate is named Deepak Bohara
statement: The associate remanded with Durga Prasai is named Deepak Bohara.
verification_note: All India Radio names the associate Dipak Khadka; the Himalayan Times page also mentions 'Deepak Khadka' in the retrieved text.

title: Prasai's arrested associate is named Dipak Khadka
statement: The associate arrested with Durga Prasai is named Dipak Khadka.
verification_note: Himalayan Times names the associate Deepak Bohara.

title: President Ram Chandra Paudel resigned on 9 September 2025
statement: President Ram Chandra Paudel resigned on 9 September 2025.
verification_note: The Week, citing AFP and ANI, reports the army said the President had not resigned. No retrievable source supports the rumour.

title: Prison department figure of 13,591 escaped inmates and 964 children (19 September 2025)
statement: The director of the Department of Prison Management, Chomendra Neupane, said on 19 September 2025 that 13,591 of 29,212 inmates and 964 of 1,422 children had escaped, with 8,816 still unaccounted for.
figure_more: of 29,212 inmates; 964 of 1,422 children escaped; 8,816 still unaccounted for
verification_note: Police gave 14,507 inmates on 11 September. Neupane's figure is a later count by the prison authority.

title: 14,507 inmates escaped (Nepal Police, 11 Sept)
statement: Onlinekhabar reported Nepal Police said 14,507 inmates had escaped from prisons nationwide, with 573 detainees having fled from police custody.
verification_note: Differs from the 13,500 figure Nepal Police gave a day earlier and from later Department of Prison Management totals.

title: 14,549 prisoners escaped (Department of Prison Management, 26 Sept)
statement: Himalaya Press, citing Department of Prison Management director Chomendra Neupane, reported 14,549 inmates escaped from 37 facilities, 8,054 had returned and 6,494 were at large.
verification_note: Conflicts with the 14,558 total and 7,735 returned reported by PTI two days later.

title: 14,558 prisoners escaped (Department of Prison Management, 28 Sept)
statement: PTI, citing the Prison Management Department, reported a total of 14,558 prisoners escaped the detention centres across the country during the protests of 8 and 9 September; 7,735 had returned and 6,813 were still absconding.
verification_note: The Department's own totals vary across dates and outlets: 14,555 (19 Sept, 13,591 plus 964 children), 14,549 (26 Sept) and 14,558 (28 Sept).

title: More than 13,500 prisoners escaped (Nepal Police, 10 Sept)
statement: Nepal Police spokesman Binod Ghimire said more than 13,500 prisoners escaped from jails across the country.
verification_note: Later figures from the Department of Prison Management are 14,549 to 14,558, and PTI quoting the Kathmandu Post gives over 15,000.

title: More than 15,000 prisoners escaped (Kathmandu Post via PTI, 11 Sept)
statement: PTI, quoting the Kathmandu Post, reported over 15,000 inmates had fled from more than 25 prisons, while the Department of Prison Management was still compiling final figures.
verification_note: Higher than every official total published later (14,549 to 14,558).

title: 12,533 prisoners still at large (12 Sept)
statement: Al Jazeera reported about 13,500 prisoners had escaped, some had been recaptured, and 12,533 were still at large.
verification_note: One source retrieved. AFP carried the same figure ('more than 12,500').

title: 6,494 prisoners still at large (Himalaya Press, 26 Sept)
statement: Himalaya Press reported 6,494 inmates at large, 5,872 from prisons and 622 from correction centres.
verification_note: Conflicts with 6,813 at large reported by PTI on 28 September, although the returned count was lower then (7,735 vs 8,054).

title: 6,813 prisoners still absconding (PTI, 28 Sept)
statement: PTI reported 6,813 prisoners were still absconding from different jails after 7,735 returned.
verification_note: Himalaya Press gave 6,494 at large on 26 September, a lower number two days earlier; the Kathmandu Post gave more than 6,800 on 25 September.

title: Private-sector loss of NPR 80 to 100 billion (FNCCI)
statement: FNCCI president Chandra Prasad Dhakal told Prime Minister Sushila Karki that initial estimates put damage at NPR 80 billion to NPR 100 billion; Kantipur reports about NPR 80 billion of private property.
figure_more: FNCCI initial estimate NPR 80 to 100 billion; Kantipur about NPR 80 billion
verification_note: AFP reports losses of NPR 25 billion; economists quoted by the Kathmandu Post estimate collateral damage near NPR 3 trillion.

title: Protests began on 1 September at Tribhuvan University
statement: A timeline on RealShePower says student protests began at Tribhuvan University on 1 September 2025 under a "Youth Against Corruption" collective and that police used tear gas. No other retrieved source reports it.
verification_note: Not corroborated by any other source retrieved. Onlinekhabar says there was no public discussion of a protest date until 6 September. Nepali Times traces the #youthsagainstcorruption campaign to Hami Nepal and the 8 September rally. The same article contains other claims that conflict with mainstream reporting (see related claims), so treat it as unreliable.

title: Protesters said their grievance was corruption and nepotism, not only the ban
statement: Global Voices reports that protesters stressed their core grievance was systemic corruption and nepotism, and that international media wrongly cast the movement as being about the ban itself.
verification_note: Written after the protests; not checked against other reporting.

title: Claim that protesters wanted Narendra Modi or Yogi Adityanath as their leader
statement: Indian posts and channels claimed that Nepali protesters wanted a leader like Narendra Modi or Yogi Adityanath, or that they demanded Modi as their prime minister.
verification_note: Assessment: false. The Quint says neither claim reflected reality on the ground; Decode (BOOM) reports that a student protester called the Modi claim 'utterly absurd and laughable'. The banner photo is covered by claim:yogi-adityanath-poster-photo-shown-as-from-nepal-gen-z-protests.

title: Report that Rajyalaxmi Chitrakar died of burns on 9 Sep
statement: Media reports on 9 September 2025 said the wife of former prime minister Jhalanath Khanal died of burns after protesters set their house on fire.
verification_note: Alt News (12 Sep) says she was alive and recovering, ANI (11 Sep) says critical; many Indian outlets had reported her dead. Her later status is not in the cited sources.

title: Ramechhap prison, 11 Sep: three inmates killed
statement: Three inmates were killed and 13 injured in a clash at Ramechhap District Prison on 11 September 2025, per a police source quoted by ANI.
verification_note: Himalayan Times and Setopati, citing the Army, say two killed and 12 injured.

title: Ramechhap prison, 11 Sep: two inmates killed
statement: Two inmates were killed and 12 injured when the Nepal Army opened fire during an attempted break-out at Ramechhap District Prison on 11 September 2025.
verification_note: Himalayan Times and Setopati cite the Army; ANI (Tribune) says three killed and 13 injured.

title: Registration deadline expired Wednesday night, 3 September
statement: The seven-day registration window ended on Wednesday 3 September 2025. The Himalayan Times says it expired on Thursday at midnight, and Radio Nepal's notice report gives 4 September. Counting seven days from 28 August gives 4 September.
verification_note: Four outlets give 3 September (Wednesday); Himalayan Times gives Thursday at midnight; Radio Nepal gives 4 September. The notice itself was not retrieved.

title: Government: the registration rule aims at accountability and monitoring
statement: The government said the regulation aims to ensure accountability, improve monitoring of online content and curb misuse of social media, while allowing access to verified and secure platforms.
verification_note: Official aim as reported; CPJ and journalists' bodies disputed the broader approach.

title: Relief for victims' families: Rs 1 million or Rs 1.5 million
statement: Karki announced on 14 September that families of those killed would each receive one million rupees; Setopati reported on 15 September a cabinet decision of Rs 1.5 million per family, including Rs 1 million as relief and Rs 500,000 for other expenses.
verification_note: Possibly different items (relief versus total package) but sources frame it as the same payment. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'confirmed': Possibly different items (relief against the total package); no incompatible account is established.

title: Indian TV claim that rioters tried to vandalise Pashupatinath Temple before the army deployed
statement: A Zee News anchor said that rioters hiding within the crowd of protesters attempted to vandalise Pashupatinath Temple and that the army was deployed only after this incident. Other Indian outlets aired the same footage as an attack on the temple.
verification_note: Assessment: false. A temple monk told AFP that everything was peaceful inside the temple. The footage was an older ritual, see claim:video-shows-protesters-storming-pashupatinath-temple.

title: Supreme Court registration ruling dated 17 August 2025
statement: The Supreme Court ruling that required registration of social media platforms was delivered on 17 August 2025.
verification_note: Likely a confusion with the date the Kathmandu Post published the full text (17 Aug 2025); not verified. Source text was not retrieved verbatim.

title: Supreme Court registration verdict dated 29 September 2024
statement: The Supreme Court extended bench delivered its verdict on mandatory registration of online and social media platforms on 29 September 2024.
verification_note: Conflicts with the CPJ reference to an '17 August' ruling.

title: Shooting continued after curfew order
statement: Firing and bloodshed continued on Baneshwar's streets after the curfew order was issued.
verification_note: Kantipur: blood still flowing after the order. HRW places lethal force until about 4 pm and Kathmandu Post says few in the crowd heard the order.

title: Sikkim rally video shown as Nepali protesters chanting for a Hindu nation or Modi
statement: A video of a rally with 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' slogans was shared as Nepali protesters demanding a Hindu nation, calling for India's Hindu nation or marching in support of Narendra Modi.
verification_note: Assessment: false. BOOM, Alt News and Digiteye each place the video in Sikkim. Their accounts of which Sikkim event it shows differ, see claim:sikkim-video-origin-event-conflict.

title: Which Sikkim event the 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' video shows
statement: Fact-checkers agree the video is from Sikkim but name different events: a rally attended by Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang on the eve of Independence Day, an Independence Day rally in Gangtok on 15 August 2025, or the 50th statehood anniversary celebrations on 29 May 2025.
verification_note: BOOM: rally attended by the Sikkim chief minister on the eve of Independence Day. Alt News: Independence Day rally in Gangtok, 15 August 2025. Digiteye: 29 May 2025, Sikkim's 50th statehood anniversary, with a PIB report as support. The sources do not resolve the difference.

title: Social Media Bill introduced on Monday 27 January 2025
statement: The government introduced the Social Media Bill in the National Assembly on Monday, reported on 29 to 30 January (27 Jan, derived).
verification_note: 27 Jan is derived from 'on Monday' in a Himalayan Times report dated 29/30 Jan.

title: Social Media Bill tabled on 29 January 2025
statement: Communications Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung tabled the Social Media Bill in the National Assembly on 29 January 2025.
verification_note: See the 27 Jan and 9 Feb claims.

title: Social Media Bill presented on 9 February 2025
statement: The communications minister presented the social media bill in the National Assembly on 9 February 2025.
verification_note: CPJ gives the date in its text; Kantipur's headline of 9 Feb says the bill 'was submitted'. The bill was already under public criticism on 30 Jan, so this date may refer to a later step.

title: The Social Media Bill threatens freedom of expression
statement: Journalists' federations, digital-law experts and CPJ said the Social Media Bill threatens freedom of expression and press freedom.
verification_note: Four publishers carry the criticism. The government's stated aim of regulation is reported separately.

title: Sudan Gurung is not a Nepali citizen
statement: Rumours said protest leader Sudan Gurung was not a Nepali citizen but from Darjeeling. Gen Z fact-checkers released a copy of his Nepali citizenship card in the Discord room and on social media.
verification_note: Debunking reported by Al Jazeera only; the card image itself was not retrieved.

title: Sudan Gurung took leadership of the crowd at Everest Hotel around noon
statement: The NHRC investigation report, as reported by HimalPress, says Sudan Gurung of Hami Nepal took leadership of the crowd in front of Everest Hotel at about 12 pm on 8 September, after which protesters broke through barricades. It also says coordinators including Rakshya Bam and Jasmine Ojha argued with him at Maitighar around 9 am and asked him to withdraw.
verification_note: Single report of the NHRC findings; the report itself was not retrieved. Hami Nepal posted on 7 September that it was not there to lead, and Gurung later said he was not the leader. Report date not shown on the page.

title: About 20,000 Supreme Court case files lost (SCMP)
statement: SCMP, as summarised in a search result, reports an estimated 20,000 case files, many without digital backups, were lost at the Supreme Court, and that blazes incinerated more than 450,000 court files overall.
figure_more: more than 450,000 court files burned overall
verification_note: SCMP's page returned 403 and only the search snippet was available, so no date or quote is recorded. Setopati gives more than 60,000.

title: More than 60,000 Supreme Court case files burned (Setopati)
statement: Setopati's field report states more than 60,000 case files were burned at the Supreme Court.
verification_note: SCMP reports about 20,000 Supreme Court case files lost.

title: Government says the block enforces a Supreme Court directive
statement: The government says the block follows a Supreme Court directive to list and monitor online platforms. Critics, including a Nepali Congress general secretary, say the court asked for legal mechanisms, not a shutdown by directive.
verification_note: The directive text was not retrieved. Kathmandu Post and Himalayan Times report the government link; Gagan Thapa and an Onlinekhabar opinion piece dispute that the order authorises a block without a parliamentary law.

title: Tear gas fired from elevated positions
statement: Tear gas grenades were fired from elevated positions, some in and around hospital premises.
verification_note: Amnesty; the Australian page is a copy of the same release.

title: Telegram ban may have followed refusal to share user data
statement: The ban may have resulted from Telegram's alleged refusal to hand over user data to Nepali authorities (reports cited by Access Now).
verification_note: Access Now says "reports suggest"; no primary source retrieved.

title: Telegram blocked to combat online fraud and money laundering
statement: Nepal said the Telegram block was aimed at combating online fraud and money laundering.
verification_note: Access Now reports that the ban may instead have followed Telegram's alleged refusal to hand over user data.

title: Thapa-led Congress is the legitimate party
statement: The Election Commission decided on 16 January 2026 to recognise the Gagan Thapa-led Nepali Congress as legitimate; the Deuba camp rejected the ruling.
verification_note: The Deuba camp says it will contest the ruling on legal, political and constitutional grounds; later recognition by the Supreme Court is mentioned in a search summary only.

title: Thousands of prisoners freed
statement: Thousands of prisoners were freed after attacks on jails on 9 September.
verification_note: No count given by HRW. Compare 14,555 (commission) and nearly 900 in two prisons (Fox). Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': The note records that HRW gives no count; no source disputes the claim.

title: Three police officers killed on 9 Sep
statement: Three police officers were beaten to death by mobs in Kathmandu on 9 September 2025.
verification_note: HRW (pathologists, police officials), The Kathmandu Post (Army data), Nepal Police via ANI, and the Chief Secretary all give three.

title: TikTok was banned in 2023 for disrupting social harmony
statement: The Dahal government banned TikTok in November 2023, saying it disrupted social harmony, goodwill and family and social relations, and spread indecent material.
verification_note: Official reason as reported; the claim records the stated reason, not its truth.

title: Tinkune violence: 45 injured
statement: Two people died and 45 were injured in the clashes at Tinkune on 28 March 2025.
verification_note: Reports differ on injuries: 45 (Kathmandu Post), 'hundreds' (IANS, 8 Apr). Retrieved reports do not say how each was counted.

title: Tinkune violence: hundreds injured
statement: The 28 March Tinkune violence left two dead and hundreds injured.
verification_note: Contradicts the 45 figure published on 28 March.

title: Tinkune turnout was 'hardly 5,000'
statement: The 28 March pro-monarchy demonstration drew 'hardly 5,000' people.
verification_note: Kathmandu Post estimate; the 9 March airport rally was put at 10,000 by Al Jazeera.

title: Toll: at least 29 dead by 10 September
statement: At least 29 people were killed during the youth-led protests against the social media restrictions (The Record, 10 September).
verification_note: Conflicts with 19 deaths reported for 8 September by most outlets and with more than 50 by 12 September (UN News); The Record gives no breakdown by day. No verbatim anchor retrieved. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': 29 on 10 September fits the Ministry's 30 on the same date; the earlier conflict named is a different date.

title: Toll: at least 76 dead over 8-9 September
statement: At least 76 people were killed during the 8-9 September 2025 protests, with more than 2,000 injured nationwide (Amnesty).
verification_note: HRW, Amnesty and OCCRP (reporting NHRC) give the same total.

title: Toll eight dead
statement: At least eight people had died in Kathmandu after police opened fire.
verification_note: Himal Press interim count: five at Civil Hospital and three at the Trauma Centre in that article.

title: Toll fourteen dead
statement: Fourteen people had died after police opened fire, by 4 pm on Monday.
verification_note: Kathmandu Post interim count as republished by ANN: 7 Trauma Centre, 3 Everest, 2 Civil, 1 KMC, 1 TUTH.

title: Toll: more than 50 dead by 12 September
statement: More than 50 people had died in the crackdown on the youth-led protests by 12 September 2025.
verification_note: UN News figure. Not a conflict with 19 (8 September) or 76 (final): counts rose over the days.

title: Toll nineteen nationwide
statement: Nineteen people died on 8 September: 17 in Kathmandu and 2 in Itahari.
verification_note: Kathmandu Post, ANI/Tribune, All India Radio, Al Jazeera, HRW and others. All India Radio's split (16 Valley, 2 Itahari) adds to 18 and conflicts with its own total of 19.

title: Toll one dead early afternoon
statement: One protester had died at Civil Hospital in New Baneshwor.
verification_note: ANI report updated 02:40 pm IST (about 3:25 pm Nepal time). Early figure; superseded the same day.

title: Toll seventeen dead in kathmandu
statement: At least 17 people were killed in Kathmandu on 8 September.
verification_note: Himal Press, Kathmandu Post (17 plus 2 in Itahari) and HRW agree on 17 in Kathmandu.

title: Toll six dead
statement: The death toll in the capital rose to six: four at the Trauma Centre, one at Civil Hospital, one at Kathmandu Medical College.
figure_more: 4 at the National Trauma Centre; 1 at Civil Hospital; 1 at Kathmandu Medical College
verification_note: Onlinekhabar interim count. Onlinekhabar says deaths were from rubber bullets (see claim early-deaths-from-rubber-bullets).

title: Toll two dead mid afternoon
statement: Two protesters had been killed in Kathmandu.
verification_note: ANI report updated 3:20 pm IST. One died at Civil Hospital and one at a trauma centre. Superseded by later counts.

title: Losses estimated at NPR 25 billion (AFP)
statement: AFP reported losses were estimated at 25 billion Nepali rupees ($177 million), with more than 2,000 workers affected.
figure_more: US$177 million; more than 2,000 workers affected
verification_note: FNCCI reports NPR 80 to 100 billion; the Hotel Association alone reports NPR 25 billion for hotels.

title: Two of the 19 deaths on 8 September were in Jhapa
statement: The commission report as quoted by the Kathmandu Post says 19 demonstrators died on 8 September, 17 in Kathmandu and two in Jhapa.
figure_more: 19 demonstrators died on 8 September; 17 in Kathmandu
verification_note: Other entries in this dataset place the two deaths outside the capital at Itahari. The retrieved text does not explain the difference.

title: CPJ: Kantipur Media Group and Annapurna Post offices set on fire
statement: Protesters set fire to the offices of Kantipur Media Group and the daily Annapurna Post on 9 September.
verification_note: CPJ counts these two; RSF counts more than a dozen outlets attacked; FNJ counts 26 incidents. Different scopes rather than a direct conflict. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': CPJ, RSF and FNJ cover different scopes; not a direct conflict.

title: UML chair should resign after the election defeat
statement: Yogesh Bhattarai and General Secretary Shankar Pokharel's report argue Oli should step down; Vice-chair Ram Bahadur Thapa's report argues the general convention's mandate is not undone by one election result.
verification_note: Internal party dispute; Oli had said he would not give up the chair, per a search summary.

title: Valley sixteen and itahari two
statement: Sixteen of the dead were in Kathmandu Valley and two in Itahari; forensic experts received 16 bodies for autopsy.
figure_more: 2 more in Itahari; forensic experts received 16 bodies for autopsy
verification_note: All India Radio gives 16 + 2 = 18 while stating 19; Onlinekhabar (9 Sept) says 16 bodies were received for autopsy. The Kathmandu Post, Himal Press and HRW give 17 in Kathmandu.

title: Viral video: gate-breaking shows Nepal protest
statement: A video of protesters breaking gates was shared as Nepal's September 2025 protests.
verification_note: BOOM traced it to Pati Square, Central Java, Indonesia, August 2025.

title: Video of a man dragged into a river said to show Finance Minister Bishnu Paudel
statement: A video of a man allegedly beaten and dragged into a river by protesters was shared by media outlets and on social media as showing Finance Minister Bishnu Paudel.
verification_note: Media Diversity Institute reports that a fact-check found the man was not the finance minister; the underlying fact-check was not retrieved. Newslaundry (9 September) separately states that Deputy PM and Finance Minister Bishnu Paudel was beaten up by protesters, so the identity of this one video is contested, not the attack on the minister.

title: Viral video: Khagrachhari violence against army
statement: A video was shared claiming hill people were attacking the army and BGB in Khagrachhari.
verification_note: Dismislab geolocated it to Gaushala Police Circle in Kathmandu using Google Street View.

title: Viral video: protest in Ladakh
statement: A video was shared as showing a protest in Ladakh.
verification_note: Newschecker placed it at the Chitwan district administration office on 9 September 2025.

title: Viral video: protest in the Philippines
statement: A clip was shared as showing a rally in the Philippines.
verification_note: VERA Files traced it to a TikTok video posted 8 September 2025 in Kathmandu.

title: Viral video: protesters storm Pashupatinath Temple
statement: A viral video was shared as showing Nepal protesters storming Pashupatinath Temple.
verification_note: BOOM traced it to the Basleshwari jatra festival, March 2025.

title: 9 September violence followed live-streamed casualty videos
statement: The commission concluded that videos of casualties and police repression in Baneshwor on 8 September, broadcast live on social media, preceded the escalation to extreme violence on 9 September.
verification_note: Taken from a search-result summary of the Ratopati page; the fetched text did not repeat it, so no quote is attached.

title: 2,522 wounded per the commission report
statement: A total of 76 people were killed and 2,522 wounded during two days of unrest, per Reuters's reading of the commission report.
verification_note: Differs from the later 2,660 verified injured. Status was 'disputed' with no dispute link; set to 'single-source': The commission's March 2026 tally; the May 2026 list of 2,660 is a later update.

title: 14 writ petitions received on 15 October
statement: The Supreme Court received 14 writ petitions on 15 October 2025, ten of them on House dissolution and government formation.
verification_note: Conflicts with All India Radio's 14 October date and 'more than seven' count; the two may count different periods.

title: Photo of Yogi Adityanath poster shown as from the Gen Z protests
statement: A photo of a poster of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was shared with the caption 'GenZ in Nepal wants something we already have', implying protesters carried it in September 2025.
verification_note: Assessment: false. BOOM found the photo dates to 9 March 2025, at a pro-monarchy rally by the Rastriya Prajatantra Party welcoming former King Gyanendra Shah at Tribhuvan International Airport.
